1	# Stage 03: Custom Analysis
2	
3	## Purpose
4	Run a user-defined analysis on artifacts the earlier stages produced — the one stage whose
5	content is designed in dialogue rather than fixed by a contract. The control that makes this
6	safe is a **plan file**: the agent drafts `PLAN.md` as a reviewable document, a person approves
7	it, and only the approved plan executes. Intent gets a human gate exactly the way the design
8	table did in stage 01.
9	
10	**The rails are not yours.** `_system/stage03_analysis.py` allocates the analysis directory,
11	enforces the approval gate, verifies the declared outputs and writes `OUTPUTS.tsv`, `STATUS`
12	and the history entry. Your judgment goes into the *content* of the plan and the scripts that
13	implement it — nowhere else. See `docs/decisions/0026-stage-03-is-plan-gated.md` in the GARS
14	repository for why.
15	
16	## Inputs
17	- Working (this run): the project (`projects/<project_title>/`), the user's stated goal, and
18	  the artifacts resolvable through `_system/resolve_artifact.py` — never paths guessed or
19	  remembered.
20	- Reference (every run):
21	  - `_references/artifact_types.md` — the closed vocabulary the plan's Outputs table may use
22	  - `_system/stage03_analysis.py` — the rails: `create`, `approve`, `verify`
23	  - `_system/resolve_artifact.py` — how every input is found
24	  - `_system/gars-env.sh` — the execution environment (`gars-bio` unless the plan says otherwise)
25	
26	## Scope Boundaries
27	The failure this stage is built around: an ungoverned agent, asked for "a quick look at the
28	data", improvising an analysis nobody reviewed and nobody can reproduce.
29	
30	- Do **not** execute anything — no script, notebook, one-liner, or skill — before
31	  `stage03_analysis.py approve` has succeeded on the plan. Drafting is free; running is gated.
32	- Do **not** run `approve` before the user has read the plan and said yes to it. The command
33	  records an approval that happened in dialogue; it never substitutes for one.
34	- Do **not** resolve an input any way other than `resolve_artifact.py`. No globbing around
35	  `02_bioinformatics/`, no paths recalled from earlier turns.
36	- Do **not** write outside this analysis's own directory
37	  (`03_custom_analysis/<NN_slug>/`). Inputs are read-only; upstream artifacts are never
38	  modified, moved, or "fixed".
39	- Do **not** edit `PLAN.md` after approval. A change of mind is a new analysis — run `create`
40	  again; the superseded one keeps its record.
41	- Do **not** install anything (`pip`, `conda`, `mamba`). If the method needs a tool the
42	  environments lack, the plan is blocked on that fact: say so and stop.
43	- Do **not** re-run, repair, or substitute for a stage 02 sub-stage. If the needed artifact is
44	  missing, resolution fails and that is the report.
45	- Do **not** interpret results beyond what the plan's Goal asks. The templates report what was
46	  produced; the science of what it *means* is the user's.
47	
48	## Definitions
49	**Analysis.** One directory `03_custom_analysis/<NN_slug>/`, holding `PLAN.md`, `scripts/`,
50	`results/`, and after completion `OUTPUTS.tsv` + `STATUS`. `NN` is allocated by `create`, in
51	order; a project accumulates analyses the way it accumulates history.
52	
53	**Plan.** `PLAN.md`: Goal, Inputs, Method, Outputs, Execution. Drafted by you from the user's
54	words and the resolvable artifacts; it is the record of intent, and after approval it is
55	frozen. The skeleton's `<FILL: ...>` markers name what each section must contain — `approve`
56	refuses while any marker survives, so an empty plan cannot slip through on charm.
57	
58	**Approved.** `PLAN.md` carries `Status: APPROVED <date>` **and** `PLAN.md.approved` sits beside
59	it, both written by `approve` after its gates pass: no skeleton markers, a non-empty Outputs
60	table, every output type in the closed vocabulary, every output path relative. The record binds
61	the approval to the plan's sha256 as stamped, so `verify` refuses a plan that was edited after
62	approval, and refuses a `Status: APPROVED` line that `approve` did not write (decision 0042).
63	Approval is durable — it lives in the files, not in the conversation. `PLAN.md.approved` is
64	machine-owned: never write, edit, copy or move it.
65	
66	**Execution venue.** The plan's Execution section opens with a `Runs:` line, and `approve`
67	refuses any value outside this vocabulary: `Runs: batch` — the workspace's configured
68	executor (`_config/executor.yaml`, decision 0039; Slurm on this cluster), the default for
69	**every** analysis, whatever its size — or `Runs: login-node (user-requested)`, allowed only
70	when the user explicitly asked for login-node execution in this analysis's dialogue. `sbatch`
71	is accepted as `batch`'s Slurm-era spelling and means exactly the same thing, so every plan
72	already written on the cluster still approves. Whether a job is
73	"small enough" for the login node is not a judgment this stage makes: the login node's cgroup
74	kills whatever is running when memory runs short, not whatever is at fault, and a wrong size
75	estimate is exactly the mistake a default cannot make (decision 0027).
76	
77	**Complete.** `verify` exit 0: every declared output exists and is non-empty, `OUTPUTS.tsv`
78	and `STATUS` are written. An analysis whose outputs are missing is FAILED, whatever the
79	scripts' exit codes claimed.
80	
81	## Process
82	1. Activated when the user asks for a custom or downstream analysis of an existing project.
83	   Identify the project; run
84	   `python3 _system/resolve_artifact.py --project projects/<title> --assay <Assay ID> --list`
85	   for the relevant assay. If nothing is resolvable — no completed sub-stage declares any
86	   artifact and stage 01 has emitted nothing — reply T1 and stop.
87	2. Run `python3 _system/stage03_analysis.py create --project projects/<title> --slug <slug>`,
88	   with a short kebab-case slug named after the goal.
89	3. Draft the plan: replace every `<FILL: ...>` marker in the created `PLAN.md`. Inputs come
90	   from step 1's resolution; Outputs use the closed vocabulary, preferring a specific type
91	   (`counts_gene`, `de_results`, …) over a generic one (`table`, `figure`, `report`) wherever
92	   one fits; Execution keeps its `Runs: batch` line unless the user explicitly asked for the
93	   login node. This is the step where your judgment belongs — spend it here, not at the
94	   keyboard later.
95	4. Reply T2 and stop. The user reads the plan, edits it if they wish, and answers.
96	5. If the user asks for changes, apply them to `PLAN.md` (it is still DRAFT), then reply T2
97	   again with what changed. If they decline the analysis, stop; the DRAFT directory remains as
98	   the record that it was considered.
99	6. On the user's approval, run
100	   `python3 _system/stage03_analysis.py approve --project projects/<title> --analysis <NN_slug>`.
101	   Exit 2 → the plan is not actually complete: reply T3 with the `blocked` reasons, fix the
102	   plan (that is a draft edit, allowed), and return to step 4. Never argue past the gate.
103	7. Execute the approved plan literally: write the scripts it describes under `scripts/` and
104	   submit them through the executor door —
105	   `python3 <workspace>/_system/executorlib.py submit --workspace <project dir> <script>` —
106	   in the environment the plan names; a login-shell run happens only when the plan's `Runs:`
107	   line reads `login-node (user-requested)`. On submission reply
108	   T4 and monitor the job. Steps not in the plan do not happen.
109	8. If execution fails, write `STATUS` as `FAILED <iso8601>`, reply T5 with the actual error,
110	   and stop. Do not patch around the failure and re-run: diagnosis goes to the user, and a
111	   changed method is a new plan.
112	9. On execution success, run
113	   `python3 _system/stage03_analysis.py verify --project projects/<title> --analysis <NN_slug> --model "<model id>"`.
114	   `--model` is the exact model id you are running as (decision 0024); omit only if you cannot
115	   name it. Exit 1 → declared outputs are missing or empty: write `STATUS` as `FAILED`, reply
116	   T5, stop. Exit 2 → the plan was never approved; treat as step 8's failure — something ran
117	   that should not have.
118	10. Exit 0 → append the returned `history_entry` to the project's `HISTORY.md` **verbatim**,
119	    replacing `<ISO-8601 date>` with today's date, and reply T6.
120	
121	## Response Format
122	Every message you send in this stage is one of the templates below, with placeholders filled.
123	Add nothing else: no observations, no suggestions, no interpretation of results.
124	
125	One standing exception, from `_references/contract_standard.md` ("the bounded voice"): if the
126	user asks a direct question, answer it from this workspace's own files — the contracts,
127	`_references/`, and the current project's directory — read-only, in a short paragraph, then
128	restate the pending wait point. Never let the answer become an action, a recommendation to
129	deviate, or a reason to skip a step.
130	
131	**T1 — Nothing to analyse**
132	```
133	Stage 03 needs artifacts from the earlier stages, and none are resolvable in
134	projects/<project_title>/ yet:
135	
136	<resolver problems / skipped sub-stages, verbatim>
137	
138	Complete the stage named above first; its artifacts will then resolve here by type.
139	```
140	
141	**T2 — Plan ready for review**
142	```
143	Analysis plan drafted: projects/<project_title>/03_custom_analysis/<NN_slug>/PLAN.md
144	
145	Goal: <the Goal section's first sentence>
146	Inputs: <n> artifact(s) — <types, comma-separated>
147	Outputs: <n> declared — <types, comma-separated>
148	Execution: <login node | batch>, per the plan.
149	
150	Read the plan file — Goal, Method, Outputs. Edit anything directly, or tell me the changes.
151	Nothing runs until you approve it. Approve as written?
152	```
153	
154	**T3 — Approval blocked**
155	```
156	The approval gate refused the plan:
157	
158	<blocked reasons, verbatim>
159	
160	I will fix the plan and show it to you again.
161	```
162	
163	**T4 — Scheduled**
164	```
165	Analysis <NN_slug> submitted: job <jobid>, per the plan's Execution section.
166	I will report when it completes; STATUS in the analysis directory is the authority meanwhile.
167	```
168	
169	**T5 — Failed**
170	```
171	Analysis <NN_slug> FAILED at <step>:
172	
173	<the actual error, verbatim>
174	
175	STATUS records the failure. The plan is unchanged; say how you want to proceed — a revised
176	method is a new plan for your review, not a silent retry.
177	```
178	
179	**T6 — Complete**
180	```
181	Analysis <NN_slug> complete.
182	
183	| Output | Type |
184	|---|---|
185	| <path> | <type> |
186	
187	Recorded in OUTPUTS.tsv and HISTORY.md. The plan that produced this is frozen at
188	03_custom_analysis/<NN_slug>/PLAN.md.
189	```
190	
191	## OUTPUT
192	
193	| Artifact | Contents |
194	|---|---|
195	| `03_custom_analysis/<NN_slug>/PLAN.md` | the approved plan — goal, inputs, method, outputs, execution; the record of intent |
196	| `03_custom_analysis/<NN_slug>/scripts/` | every script the analysis ran, exactly as run |
197	| `03_custom_analysis/<NN_slug>/results/` | the outputs the plan declared |
198	| `03_custom_analysis/<NN_slug>/OUTPUTS.tsv` | declared artifacts by type, written by `verify` |
199	| `03_custom_analysis/<NN_slug>/STATUS` | `COMPLETE <iso8601>` or `FAILED <iso8601>` — the only authority |
200	| `HISTORY.md` entry | template version, model, plan reference, goal, outputs |
201	
202	## Human check
203	Open `PLAN.md` before approving and read Goal, Method and Outputs. Approve only if it is the
204	analysis you asked for, computed the way you would defend in a lab meeting — approval is the
205	moment your intent freezes, and everything after it is mechanical.
206

# Artifact Types

The closed vocabulary a sub-stage may use to declare what it produced. A sub-stage records its
artifacts in `OUTPUTS.tsv`; a later sub-stage finds its inputs by type instead of by hardcoded
path.

**Closed means closed.** A sub-stage that needs a type not listed here stops and asks for the
vocabulary to be extended. Inventing a type defeats the point: the value is that a consumer can
rely on a name meaning one thing.

## Vocabulary

| Type | Contents | Typical producer |
|---|---|---|
| `samplesheet` | Workflow-ready sample manifest, assay-specific columns | 01_prepare_samplesheets |
| `design` | `sample_id,condition,group,replicate`, one row per sample | 01_prepare_samplesheets |
| `counts_gene` | Gene-level count matrix, genes x samples | 02.01 |
| `counts_transcript` | Transcript-level count matrix | 02.01 |
| `tpm_gene` | Gene-level TPM matrix | 02.01 |
| `bam_genome` | Coordinate-sorted, deduplicated genome alignments | 02.01 |
| `bam_transcriptome` | Transcriptome-space alignments | 02.01 |
| `vcf` | Variant calls | variant-calling sub-stages |
| `h5ad` | AnnData single-cell matrix | single-cell sub-stages |
| `de_results` | Differential expression table, one row per gene | 02.02 |
| `qc_multiqc` | Aggregated MultiQC HTML report | 02.01 |
| `gene_id_map` | Identifier translation table, e.g. `gene_id` -> `gene_name` | any adapter |
| `peaks` | Per-sample peak calls (MACS2 narrowPeak/broadPeak set) | ATAC/ChIP-family 02.01 |
| `peaks_consensus` | Consensus peak set across all samples (BED) | ATAC/ChIP-family 02.01 |
| `counts_peaks` | Read counts over the consensus peak set, peaks x samples | ATAC/ChIP-family 02.01 |
| `bigwig` | Normalised signal tracks (bigWig set) | ATAC/ChIP-family 02.01 |
| `methylation_coverage` | Per-sample cytosine coverage (`*.bismark.cov.gz` set) | methylseq 02.01 |
| `methylation_calls` | Per-sample context-split methylation calls | methylseq 02.01 |
| `bedgraph` | Per-sample methylation bedGraph tracks | methylseq 02.01 |
| `table` | A tabular result of a custom analysis | 03_custom_analysis |
| `figure` | A plot or image produced by a custom analysis | 03_custom_analysis |
| `report` | A human-readable document (md/html/pdf) summarising an analysis | 03_custom_analysis |

The three stage-03 types are deliberately generic: a custom analysis's semantics live in its
`PLAN.md`, which sits beside its `OUTPUTS.tsv` — a consumer that needs to know *what* a `table`
contains reads the plan that produced it. The specific types above them stay preferred wherever
one fits: an analysis that produces a count matrix declares `counts_gene`, not `table`.

## OUTPUTS.tsv

Written by a sub-stage on completion, beside its `STATUS`. Tab-separated, three columns, one
row per artifact:

```
# type          role      path
counts_gene     native    run/upstream/results/star_salmon/salmon.merged.gene_counts_length_scaled.tsv
qc_multiqc      native    run/upstream/results/multiqc/star_salmon/multiqc_report.html
counts_gene     adapted   adapted/counts_gene.tsv
gene_id_map     native    adapted/gene_id_to_name.tsv
```

Paths are **relative to the sub-stage output directory**, so a project stays relocatable. They
are references, never copies — an artifact is recorded where its producer wrote it.

A path may name a **directory** when the artifact is inherently a per-sample set (`peaks`,
`bigwig`): the set is the artifact, and a consumer globs inside it. Single-file artifacts keep
single-file paths — a directory is never used to avoid naming the real file.

### The `role` column

This is the one thing the design gained from running the 02.01 -> 02.02 handoff for real.

| Role | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `native` | Exactly what the producing tool emitted. Authoritative. |
| `adapted` | A reshaping of another artifact, made to satisfy a specific consumer's input contract. |

An adaptation was unavoidable: nf-core emits `gene_id, gene_name, <samples>` while `rnaseq-de`
requires the identifier column to be named `gene` and every later column to be numeric. Without
the distinction, a registry would list two `counts_gene` artifacts with no way to tell which is
the real one — and a later consumer could silently pick a matrix reshaped for someone else's
parser.

Rules:

- An `adapted` artifact is written into the **adapting sub-stage's own directory**, never over
  the producer's output.
- Resolution prefers `native` unless a contract explicitly asks for an adaptation it created.
- An adaptation may only reshape: rename columns, drop non-essential columns, change numeric
  type. It may never filter rows, alter values, or aggregate. Anything beyond reshaping is
  analysis and belongs in a sub-stage's Process, recorded in `HISTORY.md`.

## Resolution

A sub-stage needing type T searches the `OUTPUTS.tsv` of completed sub-stages in **reverse
sub-stage order** and takes the first `native` match, unless its own contract names an
`adapted` one it produced.

If no match exists it **stops and reports**. It never regenerates the artifact itself — silent
regeneration is how a project ends up with two count matrices that disagree, and no record of
which fed which result.

The supplying sub-stage is recorded in `HISTORY.md`, so every downstream result can name where
its inputs came from.
